author: Cassiodorus

passages.original: Praedicatori enim suo nullus hoc potest debere, quod Deo; operas autem hominum, quae tamen supra fundamentum Christi aedificantur, per tribulationes et diversas necessitates hujus saeculi dicit esse purgandas : sicut Pater Augustinus in libro Enchiridion plenius expla- navit.
passages.english: For no one can owe to his preacher what [he owes] to God; but the works of men, which are nevertheless built upon the foundation of Christ, he says must be purged through tribulations and the various necessities of this world, as Father Augustine explained more fully in the book Enchiridion.
passages.notes: "operas" is read as "opera" (works), with reference to 1 Corinthians 3:12–15; the form in the text may be a misprint. "expla- navit" is read as "explanavit".

passages.original: Paulus apostolus vinctus Jesu Christi, et Timotheus frater, et reliqua. Ipsis primordiis no- mini suo conjunxit noviter passionem, et ne putare- tur aliquo delicto fuisse vinctus, addidit Christi Jesu, ut illa vincula non criminosa, sed gloriosa declara- ret; scribens Philemoni fratri et adjutori suo, cum fratre Timotheo; Appiam quoque et Archippum in eadem salutatione commemorans; sed et congrega- tionem quae in domo ejus esse videbatur, pari salu- tatione complectitur;
passages.english: "Paul, a prisoner of Jesus Christ, and Timothy [our] brother," and the rest. At the very beginning he joined to his name his recent suffering, and so that he would not be thought to have been bound for some offence, he added "of Christ Jesus," in order to declare those chains not criminal but glorious; writing to Philemon, his brother and helper, together with [his] brother Timothy; mentioning also Apphia and Archippus in the same greeting; and he embraces with an equal greeting the congregation too which was seen to be in his house;
passages.notes: "Appiam" is the Latin spelling of Apphia (Philemon 2). "noviter passionem" (literally "newly [his] suffering") is taken to refer to Paul's recent imprisonment. Words split by line breaks in the scan (no- mini, putare- tur, declara- ret, congrega- tionem, salu- tatione) have been read as whole words.
